title: An audit is complete only when the final report is published at a location outside Sky's control
content:
A.1.10.2.7.3 requires that "the final audit report must be hosted on the auditor's website or another independently verifiable location. **Internal documents, shared drives, or non-permanent links do not satisfy this requirement.**" A.1.10.2.7.4 makes the consequence explicit: "An audit is considered complete when the final audit report is published at the independently verifiable hosting location."

So completion is defined by publication, not by delivery. A report that exists in Sky's own drive, however genuine, does not complete an audit — the artifact stays blocked from "deployment, Spell inclusion, or governance vote."

This is the provenance framework from A.1.10.2.4.5.1 applied to attestations. A document Sky hosts is a document Sky can edit, and its mutability is invisible to readers; the same file on the auditor's own domain is published under the auditor's reputation, and altering it would require the auditor's cooperation. Independence is a property of custody, not of content.

The rejection of "non-permanent links" adds durability to the requirements. An audit's value is largely retrospective — read months later by a validator or an investigator asking what was known and when — and a report behind a dead link provides nothing to that reader.

A.1.10.2.7.4 also requires the responsible team to confirm "that the audited scope and commit hash match the audit request" before acceptance. Publication proves the report exists; the scope-and-hash check proves it is a report about the right code.
description: A.1.10.2.7.3 rejects internal documents, shared drives and non-permanent links; A.1.10.2.7.4 makes publication, not delivery, the completion event that unblocks the artifact.
